as ''FC Juventus București'' | ground = [[Ilie Oană Stadium|Ilie Oană]] | capacity = 15,073 | owner = Asociația Clubul Sportiv Petrolul 52 | chairman = [[Claudiu Tudor]] | mgrtitle = Head coach | manager = [[Ricardo Sousa]] | league = [[Liga I]] | season = [[2025–26 Liga I#Play-out round|2025–26]] | position = Liga I, 12th of 16 | website = {{URL|https://fcpetrolul.ro/}} | current = 2026–27 FC Petrolul Ploiești season | pattern_la1 = _blueborder | pattern_b1 = _macronpropuseco24yrb | pattern_ra1 = _blueborder | pattern_sh1 = _macronskara2223rby | leftarm1 = FFFF00 | body1 = FFFF00 | rightarm1 = FFFF00 | shorts1 = 0000FF | socks1 = FFFF00 }} '''Asociația Clubul Sportiv Petrolul 52''', commonly known as '''FC Petrolul Ploiești''' ({{IPA|ro|peˈtrolul ploˈjeʃtʲ}}), '''Petrolul Ploiești''', or simply '''Petrolul''', is a Romanian professional [[Association football|football]] [[Club (organization)|club]] based in [[Ploiești]], [[Prahova County]]. It competes in the [[Liga I]], the top tier of the [[Romanian football league system|Romanian league system]]. The team was founded in 1924 in [[Bucharest]] as ''Juventus'', following the merger of ''Triumf'' and ''Romcomit'', and won its first national championship in the [[1929–30 Divizia A|1929–30 season]]. In 1952, it relocated to the industrial city of Ploiești, and adopted the name Petrolul five years later. During this period, the club enjoyed its most successful era, securing three further league titles in [[1957–58 Divizia A|1957–58]], [[1958–59 Divizia A|1958–59]], and [[1965–66 Divizia A|1965–66]]. Petrolul Ploiești has also won the [[Cupa României]] on three occasions, most recently in the [[2012–13 Cupa României|2012–13 season]]. The team made its European debut in the [[1958–59 European Cup|1958–59 season]], facing East German side [[FC Erzgebirge Aue|Wismut Karl Marx Stadt]] in the preliminary round of the [[UEFA Champions League|European Cup]]. Overall, it has participated in 12 European campaigns, eight of which were organised by [[UEFA]]. Petrolul Ploiești's traditional colours are yellow and dark blue, a combination that has earned its players and supporters the nickname "the Yellow Wolves". It plays its home matches at the 15,073-seat [[Ilie Oană Stadium]], which was inaugurated in 2011. Its principal rivalry is with [[FC Rapid București|Rapid București]], a fixture known as the [[Primvs derby|''Primvs'' derby]]. The club also shared a short-lived [[Former Ploiești derby|local rivalry]] with [[FC Astra Giurgiu|Astra Giurgiu]] between 1998 and 2012, during the period in which Astra was based in Ploiești."}}
